children: , an optical-component supplier to AI data centers, fell 11.03% to $748.01 at 10:05 a.m. ET on November 2. The business is accelerating, but the takeover math keeps moving. Marvell's proposed acquisition would give Lumentum investors 4.5 Marvell shares for each share they hold, tying the payout's dollar value to the buyer's market performance.

The operating outlook packs a punch. Lumentum's November 2 earnings release projects fiscal second-quarter revenue of $1.575 billion to $1.625 billion, following $1.26 billion in the first quarter. That puts the $1.6 billion midpoint roughly 27% higher sequentially. Adjusted operating margin is expected to reach 45%46%, up from 42.3%. At the midpoint, that would mean another 3.2 percentage points of expansiona demanding target that could help investors assess execution while the deal awaits approval.

The GuruFocus snapshot adds some caution: Lumentum scores 70 out of 100, with growth and financial strength standing above its weaker valuation and momentum readings. It also flags three severe warning signs, though the image does not identify them. Strong operating targets could support the investment case, but they do not lock in the merger payout. The announced $1,132 reference value remains dependent on Marvell's share price; it provides no guaranteed cash floor.

title: Lumentum Stocks Drop 11% With Merger Risk Overshadowing Its $1.6 Billion Revenue Outlook
